Real services. Simulated decisions.

Exercise the same agent framework, MCP tools and shopping microservices without calling Gemini. Each run uses a disposable cart. The simulated model supplies a deterministic sequence of decisions; it does not test natural-language understanding or model reasoning.

Shop and verify

Search within a €70 budget, inspect two robots in parallel, add one, then read the actual cart to verify it.

Repeated tool use

Repeat a product lookup until the real agent framework stops execution at its six-request budget.

Retry a write

Observed execution

Nested steps show actual downstream calls. Bars show when each step ran and how long it took. A failed request does not prove that a write was rolled back.

Native evidence
Fault experiments in the repository use actual Kubernetes CPU limits, catalogue availability and the original product-route delay. They restore the deployment afterward. A simulated repeating decision verifies the execution guard; it is not evidence that a real LLM is thrashing.
